title: Post-Processing a Twilight Landscape: Multi-Exposure Blending, Layered Composition, and Light-Driven Color Grading
summary: This video lesson walks through a landscape post-production workflow focused on drone- or wide-shot scenes captured at twilight. The presenter discusses the limits of drone dynamic range, advocates bracketed exposures, and blends multiple files to preserve foreground detail while preventing sky blowout. The workflow is organized around four conceptual layers (foreground, middle ground, sky, sun beams) and uses a blur-based vignette, edge refinements, and light-painting techniques to connect the light source to the subject. The tutorial also covers color and tonal adjustments (dehaze, warmth, whites, selective color), beam adjustments, and a strong emphasis on directional lighting in post, including a black-and-white dodge/burn demonstration. Throughout, the guidance stresses careful edge handling, luminosity separation, and composition tricks such as cropping and framing to guide the eye toward the light source.

sections.title: Dynamic range, drone limits, and exposure strategy
concepts: 2.0 stops DR for drones vs cameras
sections.description: Introduces the challenge of limited drone dynamic range and the need to plan exposures (2x or cropping) to preserve foreground detail while avoiding blown highlights in the sky.

sections.title: Foreground-sky blending and multi-file merging plan
sections.description: Describes selecting the closest exposure for the foreground, then bringing in a different sky exposure. Lays groundwork for a multi-file merge and notes alignment considerations.

sections.title: Four-layer structure and initial vignette approach
concepts: painting back original through the vignette
sections.description: Outlines a four-layer workflow and demonstrates creating a dark blur vignette, then selectively painting the original image back into the vignette to restore focus on the subjects.

sections.title: Edge refinement, beam consideration, and sky color control
concepts: soft vs hard edge brush for light
sections.description: Details edge work around the light source, introduces the idea of crafting or erasing beams with brush work, and discusses adjusting the sky to support the intended light direction.

sections.title: Twilight color grading and subject-light cohesion
concepts: color grading and selective color to trees
luminosity-guided painting to direct the eye
sections.description: Focuses on intensifying light where the sun is, balancing sky and foreground with tonal shifts, and applying selective color passes to accent highlights on foliage while maintaining overall cohesion.

sections.title: Black-and-white workflow and composition decisions
concepts: desaturation preserved in RGB for dodge/burn
classic dodge and burn to shape light
sections.description: Demonstrates a black-and-white approach using desaturation to enable dodge and burn, then discusses how to direct emphasis toward the light source and balance composition through cropping and point of view.

sections.title: Wrap-up and viewer collaboration
sections.description: Concludes with final remarks on the craft, noting the potential for additional shots and collaboration.
